input.rationale: The divergence point of the open gap is now measurable rather than merely unreported: the probe records, for the flagged case, whether the isolated node still holds its acknowledged entry in its own log and whether the majority-side leader still holds its own, each compared against what that node's FSM applied. Native runs of the current harness show both entries still present in their own logs two seconds after healing (minority_log_has_entry and majority_log_has_entry true, applied_without_log false on both sides), and the flag-off control shows the isolated side never had an entry at all. So no lost acknowledged entry or applied-without-log divergence was produced in this schedule; the mechanism that would truncate a losing side's suffix is not excluded, so the gap stays open and the bounded negative is submitted for a retained receipt with its control. The four existing complete comparisons and the whole-question account are unchanged.

investigations.hypothesis: A node restarted with RestoreCommittedLogs keeps the snapshot's configuration when committed membership changes sit below the restored commit index, so its quorum arithmetic reflects an obsolete membership and it can win an election its committed configuration would forbid.
investigations.discriminator: Grow a snapshot-age three-voter cluster to five voters, restart the leader, compare the configuration index and server count with the log's latest configuration, then isolate the restarted node with one committed voter and check whether it wins with the smaller quorum while the majority side keeps a leader.

knowledge.statement: With Config.RestoreCommittedLogs enabled, a restarted node that keeps a stale smaller configuration can both win leadership on a minority of the committed configuration and acknowledge client writes concurrently with the majority side's own leader: in one execution both sides acknowledged a client write while partitioned, and the flag-off control acknowledged only on the majority side.
knowledge.conditions: Committed configuration grown from three to five voters after the restarting node's snapshot; RestoreCommittedLogs=true with a CommitTrackingLogStore; the node isolated together with one committed voter immediately after NewRaft returns, that partner also cut off from the majority side; a bounded wait for the majority side to hold its own leader before either write; two second apply timeout and two second heal settle.

gaps.question: Does a leader elected with fewer votes than the committed configuration requires reproduce reliably, under which schedule and partition order, and does the committed configuration's majority side then diverge in committed entries?

interpretations.rationale: The parent question is answered by receipt 75c355f2a4634b5193fa97e4de987fe0 (exit 0, six events, no parse loss) with receipt 3e2dd223dd5f43409c21066a1ca43175 as the earlier execution of the same declaration: with RestoreCommittedLogs on and no snapshot, the restarted node reported after_latest_index 0, after_servers 0 and after_has_vote false while after_commit_index 11 and after_last_applied 11 were restored (event index 1, versus the admission at index 0 recording before_latest_index 1 with one server), and the flag-off control kept index 1 with one voter (event index 3). The snapshot-present case in the same receipt shows the loss with a committed membership change newer than the snapshot: before shutdown the log's latest configuration was index 1227 with two servers while the snapshot sat at index 1220 with configuration index 1, and after the restart the node reported after_latest_index 1 with one server (event index 5, admission 4). Mechanism: NewRaft initialises configurations to its zero value, restoreSnapshot (api.go:655-681) is the only persistent-state producer of a configuration and the startup log scan (api.go:604-620) is the only other, but restoreFromCommittedLogs (api.go:724-754) runs first and advances lastApplied to the persisted commit index, so committed LogConfiguration entries at or below it are skipped; processLogs forwards them to the FSM without ever updating r.configurations (raft.go:1366-1391). The follow-on child question has since witnessed the multi-voter variant that this account previously listed as an open limitation: with a five-voter committed configuration and a three-voter snapshot the restarted node came back at index 1 with three servers (receipt b15f4b6c55b44402ace926204de9b826, witness index 15, control 18), and that stale configuration let it win leadership and acknowledge client writes on a minority of the committed configuration, including concurrently with the majority side's leader (receipt f0db8b71047e42df96d3e2f4f581835c, witness index 27, control 29).
counterevidence: The flag-off controls keep the committed configuration in every cited execution, isolating the recovery path rather than the restart, the stores or the applied entries.
A snapshot can supply a configuration (api.go:677-678) but only as of its configuration index, which is why the snapshot-present case needed a configuration change newer than the snapshot.
limitations: Every observation is bounded (three second majority-leader wait, five second election window, two second apply timeout, two second heal settle), so no occurrence-rate or absence bound is established.
No entry-level divergence or lost acknowledged entry is witnessed in any execution; the new bounded check reports the entries surviving in their own logs and is not a durability proof.
The scenario restarts the former leader of a cluster grown by adding voters; other roles, change types, chain orders and durable stores are not explored.
interpretations.joint_history: Receipts 75c355f2a4634b5193fa97e4de987fe0 and 3e2dd223dd5f43409c21066a1ca43175 are the parent's own executions of the same single-voter scenario (the second being the earlier execution of the same declaration before identity fields were corrected); receipts b15f4b6c55b44402ace926204de9b826 and f0db8b71047e42df96d3e2f4f581835c belong to the child multi-voter question and are cited here only for the follow-on consequence named in the revised limitations. basis.prefix: The harness boots one node with CommitTrackingLogs and a low SnapshotThreshold, repeats Apply until snapshots.List() returns a snapshot, then calls AddNonvoter, awaits its IndexFuture, and commits ten more commands so the staged commit index passes the configuration entry. interpretations.rationale: Source reading establishes the mechanism: NewRaft initialises configurations to its zero value, restoreSnapshot is the only producer that can supply a configuration from persistent state (api.go:655-681), and the only other producer is the startup log scan (api.go:610-613) starting at max(snapshotIndex, lastApplied)+1. restoreFromCommittedLogs (api.go:724-754) runs before that scan and calls setCommitIndex(commitIndex) then processLogs(commitIndex, nil); processLogs forwards LogConfiguration entries to the FSM (raft.go:1366-1391) and never updates r.configurations. With RestoreCommittedLogs enabled, every committed configuration entry at or below the restored commit index is therefore invisible to the node after restart. A native construction probe of a bootstrapped single node (CommitTrackingLogs, no snapshot, 10 applied entries) reproduced the predicted difference: with the flag on the event was {after_latest_index:0, after_servers:0, after_has_vote:false, after_commit_index:11, after_last_applied:11, before_latest_index:1, snapshots:0} and the library logged 'initial configuration: index=0 servers=[]'; with the flag off the same restart reported {after_latest_index:1, after_servers:1, after_has_vote:true}. The probe is construction feedback without a retained receipt, so the formal comparison is left to the submitted experiment. Consequence under the stated conditions: the restarted node's own membership view is the pre-restart snapshot value or empty, so runFollower's 'no known peers, aborting election' branch (raft.go:228-232) and the hasVote gate (raft.go:236-246) prevent it from campaigning, and quorumSize() is computed over a configuration that contradicts the committed log (raft.go:1087-1094). Counterevidence examined: a snapshot can legitimately supply the configuration (api.go:677-678) but only as of snapshot.ConfigurationIndex, which cannot cover a configuration committed after that snapshot; appendEntries processes only entries it newly appends (raft.go:1594-1621); leaderLoop only promotes latest to committed (raft.go:797-799). Limitations: the finding is scoped to the stated configuration and store conditions; the snapshot-present variant remains a registered gap; only a controller receipt can make this a completed comparison.

The retained receipt 99b89f1a9b634301a58130e5494d394f (exit 0) contains the four emitted events, and the two result events witness the predicted difference under identical inputs: event 1 (mode on, restore_committed_logs true, snapshots 0) reports after_latest_index 0, after_servers 0, after_has_vote false with after_commit_index 11 and after_last_applied 11, while event 3 (mode off) reports after_latest_index 1, after_servers 1, after_has_vote true. The admission events (0 and 2) confirm both cases started from before_latest_index 1 with one server, so the only difference is whether restoreFromCommittedLogs advanced lastApplied. Source reading explains the mechanism: NewRaft starts with an empty configurations struct, restoreSnapshot (api.go:655-681) is the only persistent-state producer of a configuration, and the startup log scan (api.go:610-613) is the only other producer but begins at max(snapshotIndex, lastApplied)+1; restoreFromCommittedLogs (api.go:724-754) runs first and sets lastApplied to the persisted commit index, so committed LogConfiguration entries at or below it are skipped, and processLogs never updates r.configurations (raft.go:1366-1391). The receipt s declared comparisons returned unknown rather than violated: the controller reported "No corresponding prerequisite events reached: mode_on/startup_before_restart" for both on-case comparisons and the analogous message for the off-case control, because the compared identity included phase and the admission events carry phase before_restart while the result events carry after_restart. That is a declaration defect, not missing evidence, so the raw observations are retained and a successor experiment with identity_fields [mode] is submitted for a fresh, complete comparison; no completed comparison is claimed here. interpretations.rationale: Source reading establishes the mechanism: NewRaft initialises configurations to its zero value, restoreSnapshot is the only producer that can supply a configuration from persistent state (api.go:655-681), and the only other producer is the startup log scan (api.go:610-613) starting at max(snapshotIndex, lastApplied)+1. restoreFromCommittedLogs (api.go:724-754) runs before that scan and calls setCommitIndex(commitIndex) then processLogs(commitIndex, nil); processLogs forwards LogConfiguration entries to the FSM (raft.go:1366-1391) and never updates r.configurations. With RestoreCommittedLogs enabled, every committed configuration entry at or below the restored commit index is therefore invisible to the node after restart. A native construction probe of a bootstrapped single node (CommitTrackingLogs, no snapshot, 10 applied entries) reproduced the predicted difference: with the flag on the event was {after_latest_index:0, after_servers:0, after_has_vote:false, after_commit_index:11, after_last_applied:11, before_latest_index:1, snapshots:0} and the library logged 'initial configuration: index=0 servers=[]'; with the flag off the same restart reported {after_latest_index:1, after_servers:1, after_has_vote:true}. The probe is construction feedback without a retained receipt, so the formal comparison is left to the submitted experiment. Consequence under the stated conditions: the restarted node's own membership view is the pre-restart snapshot value or empty, so runFollower's 'no known peers, aborting election' branch (raft.go:228-232) and the hasVote gate (raft.go:236-246) prevent it from campaigning, and quorumSize() is computed over a configuration that contradicts the committed log (raft.go:1087-1094).
